title: AI agents now start the shopping journey, so our store must serve them
summary: 55% of consumers use AI in product discovery (NIQ); 34% of US consumers would use GenAI for holiday gifts (Gartner). Walmart opened to outside AI agents with spending limits; Best Buy joined TikTok Shop; PC shipments fell 21% in Q3 (Counterpoint).

points.headline: AI agents are becoming a buying channel, and retailers are setting the rules
points.detail: Walmart opened to outside shopping agents with profiles and spending limits while Amazon blocks them; Meta pushes a shared agent standard. We should decide how agents read and buy from our store.

points.headline: AI discovery is mainstream among shoppers, including for holiday gifting
points.detail: 55% of consumers use AI in discovery (NIQ) and 34% of US consumers would use GenAI for gift ideas (Gartner). Product data and content must be readable by AI tools before Cyber 5.

points.headline: PC demand is falling while memory costs push prices up
points.detail: Global PC shipments dropped 21% in Q3 with a 27% Q4 decline forecast, and the memory shortage is driving record PC price inflation. We should plan pricing, promotions and inventory for thinner margins.

points.headline: Best Buy's TikTok Shop move widens the electronics channel field
points.detail: Best Buy joined TikTok Shop for its biggest holiday season yet, giving electronics shoppers a new route to buy. We should test our own presence and promotions on social commerce channels.

points.headline: Small businesses are confident and spend like heavy AI users
points.detail: Small businesses are cautious but ready to grow (Capital One), and AI power users spend like small businesses (PYMNTS). This supports device-refresh offers aimed at small-business buyers.
